subject: chemistry-1
question: Which intermolecular force acts between every pair of neighboring molecules, whether those molecules are polar or nonpolar?
explanation:
London dispersion forces arise from instantaneous fluctuations in an electron cloud that induce a matching temporary dipole in a neighboring particle. Because every atom and molecule contains electrons, dispersion is universal, while hydrogen bonding requires an H bonded to N, O, or F, dipole-dipole requires a permanent dipole, and ion-dipole requires an ion. Methane, with only 10 electrons and no permanent dipole, still condenses at about -161 degrees Celsius solely because of dispersion.

ELI-10: Electrons are constantly moving, so at any instant they can be bunched slightly to one side of a molecule. That momentary imbalance repels or attracts electrons in the molecule next door, creating a matching imbalance, and the two lopsided clouds attract. Since electrons exist in every molecule, this attraction never switches off, even in molecules with no permanent plus or minus end. The other three forces each need a special ingredient that many substances simply do not have.
